source_ambiguities.statement: The source does not explicitly state the range of tau_Q for the E_i fits in Fig. (fig:Ei_integ_Tq_KZM). The caption says 'various quench times' but does not give a numerical domain. The only explicit tau_Q range in the paper is for the vortex count scaling (10 <= tau_Q <= 1000), which may not apply to the E_i fits.

assessment: The source does support the scientific core of the proposed pair: at equilibration it reports E_i versus tau_Q for T=10^{-6} and T=1; the two fitted coefficients, exponents, and quoted uncertainties are transcribed correctly; panel (a) uses 2000 realizations, panel (b) 1000; plotted-point error bars are one standard deviation; and fits with exact independent variables use inverse-variance weighted least squares. Temperature can therefore be the hidden branch condition, while tau_Q is the public experimental control. This exact ScienceCard is nevertheless not source-closed for an executable matched case. The E_i caption states only 'various quench times' and neither the caption nor the fitted-law text gives finite tau_Q endpoints. The card imports 10 <= tau_Q <= 1000 from a separate vortex-count plot, which the source does not authorize for the E_i fits and which the card itself records as unresolved. The realization counts are also sampling metadata, not physical branch conditions. The card must fail closed rather than proceed to drafting.

issues.detail: The only explicit 10 <= tau_Q <= 1000 interval is stated for vortex count n_v in Fig. 1(c). The E_i figure caption says only 'various quench times', and the E_i fit paragraph reports the two laws without numerical endpoints. The card nevertheless uses the vortex-count interval as the control domain for both E_i claims and says each applies within a 'stated range'. This does not establish a source-supported common finite intervention domain for E_i, so the Oracle interface cannot be instantiated source-only. The card's tau_Q_domain_unspecified ambiguity correctly acknowledges this unresolved gap.

The source reports R=2000 and R=1000 as the numbers of stochastic realizations used to average the two panels, and inverse-variance weighted least squares as the fitting convention. These facts belong in each claim's statistical_basis/uncertainty provenance. By also encoding R_low, R_high, and weighted_ls as fixed conditions linked to the claims, the card risks making sample size and fitting procedure part of the hidden physical world. For this proposed pair, the branch-specific world condition is temperature (T=10^{-6} versus T=1); the differing realization counts must remain statistical metadata and must not define the mechanism or world.
